title: First big band with Gaspard and the 'Tiger Rag' rehearsal
summary: A neighbour named Gaspard needed a clarinetist, persuaded Bigard's family to let him play, and the first piece at rehearsal was 'Tiger Rag'; Bigard, reading straight four-four, could not get the dance two-four feel.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: And my first big job with a big band was fantastic. That's the one with a fellow named Gaspard and they were looking for a clarinet player. And he used to -- he lived right near my home and he used to hear me every day practicing, so he asked my folks to let me come and play with them on a night job. So they didn't want me to go, anyways, so they -- he begged them, he said he'll take good care of me and bring me home. And one night they had a rehearsal trying to help me get started with the band, and the first piece they laid on me

was 'Tiger Rag.' And when they were finished I was still playing 'Tiger Rag.' That was very embarrassing because I couldn't get that two-four time. You see, I was reading like -- I played from my studies, you know. Four-four was four-four for me and so forth, but it was split time for dance music, you know. And I had a terrible time getting that in my head and especially 'Tiger Rag,' you know. It was so fast and they had all those clarinet breaks in there. Oh, boy. By the time you came to the breaks, they were gone and I was still fiddling around with the introduction.
